title: Every PPT channel has finite entanglement-breaking index
abstract: We prove that every PPT linear map has finite entanglement-breaking index, thereby establishing the eventual entanglement-breaking property of PPT channels in full generality. Furthermore, by utilizing completely positive maps with low entanglement dimensionality, we show that a large family of PPT maps, which strictly containing the class of 2-superpositive maps, has entanglement-breaking index bounded above by 3, uniformly in the dimension. In particular, these results provide strong evidence that the PPT-cubed conjecture may hold in full generality.
summary: This paper proves a major result showing that every PPT quantum channel must eventually become entanglement-breaking. By establishing the finite entanglement-breaking index for all such channels, it strengthens conjectures about the structure of quantum operations. The methods involve advanced linear algebra applied to map theory, providing deep insights into how entanglement is lost over repeated applications of physical processes.
main_problem: The central problem is proving that every Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) quantum channel eventually becomes entanglement-breaking, establishing the eventual entanglement-breaking property for this class of channels.
main_result: The authors prove that every PPT linear map acting on a quantum system has a finite entanglement-breaking index ($	ext{nEB}(\Phi) < \infty$).
method: The proof utilizes inductive arguments, decomposing the channel $\Phi$ based on spectral properties (Perron eigenmatrices) and relating the EB index to bounds derived from specific subclasses of maps like $k$-superpositive maps.
model_or_system: The study concerns linear maps $\Phi: M_d(\mathbb{C}) 	o M_d(\mathbb{C})$ acting on quantum systems, characterized by their Choi matrix. Key concepts include PPT and Entanglement-Breaking (EB) channels.
key_observables: Entanglement-breaking index ($	ext{nEB}(\Phi)$), the structure of the Choi matrix $C\Phi$, and spectral properties like the Perron radius.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the system, and indices related to map composition (e.g., $	ext{DSP}_2, 	ext{DSP}_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on structural decompositions of the channel into components supported by projections derived from eigenvalue problems.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon defining PPT and EB maps, establishing relationships between different classes of positive maps ($	ext{SP}_k$), and culminates in proving Theorem 1.1 via induction on the dimension $d$.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental structural results about quantum operations (channels) that are crucial for understanding decoherence, channel capacity, and entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems.
